summary: Across 2014 to 2023 Instagram records, Olivia Chow consistently positions strong public services and a robust social safety net as central priorities for Toronto. Chow supports expanded childcare (including the NDP's $15/day plan and a pledge to create 3,000 spaces), school nutrition programs, after-school care, youth employment supports, and senior services. On homelessness, Chow calls the situation an emergency and pledges 24/7 respite spaces and a community-led wrap-around services fund, financed partly by higher taxes on the wealthiest. Chow pledges to open all 100 public library branches seven days a week and to increase core funding for non-profits. Chow expresses support for 2SLGBTQI+ communities, Indigenous reconciliation including action on gender-based violence, workers and union jobs, people with disabilities, and addressing child poverty and food insecurity.

key_positions.stance: Supports expanded, affordable childcare and school nutrition/after-school programs
Treats homelessness as an emergency requiring 24/7 respite, wrap-around supports, and additional shelter capacity, with community-led decision making
Supports robust, reliable public services as core to Toronto life
Supports expanded public library hours and library workers
Supports increased core funding for non-profits delivering social services
Supports 2SLGBTQI+ communities, including specific public solidarity with Trans people
Supports addressing child poverty and food insecurity through expanded school food programs
Supports services for seniors, including community housing and accessible transit
Supports workers, union jobs, and safer working conditions
Supports Indigenous reconciliation and action on gender-based violence, including MMIW inquiry
Supports hiring more people with disabilities in the city workforce
Supports youth employment programs and supports for young people in crisis

key_actions.action: Announced plan to expand Toronto Public Library hours so all 100 branches are open seven days a week
Pledged to create 24/7 respite spaces and a community-led fund for wrap-around homelessness supports
Pledged to increase core funding for non-profits, funded by asking the wealthiest to pay more
Pledged to create 3,000 childcare spaces and expand the school food program by 36,000 children
Held a press conference responding to the Vital Signs report on child poverty in Toronto
Announced a school food program expansion with Frances Lankin
Joined picket lines in solidarity with CUPE Local 233 workers at Toronto Metropolitan University
Raised awareness for 360kids, a group supporting young people in crisis
References past work on a childcare deal that made childcare more affordable and eventually $10 a day
